title: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”: the things written in the past were written for our learning today, in these last days, so we can learn how to come back to the Heavenly Father and live a righteous life. Every appliance, every toy you buy comes with instructions; God gave us this holy Bible for our instructions. This book is from the Israelites, for the Israelites, to the Israelites in these last days. That is how we know who we are, because God’s spirit is in this book and God’s spirit is in us.

“That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” We just passed a great holy day, the Day of Atonement, and every year people come to the leaders afterward with a problem they had with somebody months ago that they never let go. Some are not taking the mercy, the grace and the compassion God gives us; they take it for granted. It is time for us to wake up, come back, love each other and do this work, and we do it through these scriptures, for the great awakening of Israel.

Anything we are going through, we can go in the Bible and pull out the answer: through patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.

precepts.why:
So we might have hope: “All scripture is given by inspiration of God.” These scriptures are for our inspiration, for us to grow and get some hope. We can have joy when we read the Bible, zeal and enthusiasm; we should be uplifted when we hear the words of God going out. It is supposed to inspire you to come back and do the right thing, and remind you how you are supposed to live while you are on this earth.

It “is profitable for doctrine”, the Lord’s commandments written therein, “for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.” Righteousness is the key word: all of this is to inspire us in righteousness. Some of us hold on to the things of the past, to the old man and the old woman, and never really changed. That is why it is so quick after the Day of Atonement for people to go back to the problems they had before it: they never changed. This Bible is supposed to change you, uplift you, motivate you, exhort you, and move your spirit to do the right thing in Christ.

“That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.” You want to be perfect? If you keep the law and commandments as it is written, you will be perfect in the eyes of God. Each and every one of us in here is supposed to be throughly furnished unto all good works in the Lord. That is what the things written aforetime were written for.

sense.text:
All things that are written are written for our learning. “I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud”: all our fathers, the Israelites. The cloud they were under was not a regular cloud but a chariot of God over them, and they “all passed through the sea.”

The same things that happened back then with the Egyptians, when the Lord had to save us and deliver us out, are going to happen this time around. He is going to deliver us out of this place too, but a whole different way: he is going to deliver us from the fire that is going to come here, the thermonuclear bombs that are going to blow America off the face of the earth. We are in captivity right now, whether the Israelites know it or not, and he is going to deliver us out of that captivity.

We all went through that sea, “and were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea.” The spiritual meat is the manna he gave us. For the spiritual drink, the Lord had Moses hit that rock and water came out: “and that Rock was Christ.”

“But with many of them God was not well pleased.” It is the same today: with many of these Israelites he is not pleased, out of the truth and in this truth. Don’t think that because you have fringes and borders of blue on, you are good and safe. Some in here have secret lies and secret things going on, and the Lord is not pleased with that. “For they were overthrown in the wilderness.”

“Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” Our forefathers lusted after evil things in the wilderness, doing things they had no business doing, making golden calves. They were idolaters worshipping those calves: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” Some were idolaters and others were out there committing fornication, and “fell in one day three and twenty thousand”, 23,000 in one day. They tempted Christ “and were destroyed of serpents”, and they murmured, murmuring about Moses, Aaron and Miriam, “and were destroyed of the destroyer.”

“They are written for our admonition”, for our warning, “upon whom the ends of the world are come.” That means the same people are back today: the same people with fringes and borders of blue, the same idolaters, the same fornicators, the same murmurers are back on this earth. They were left for our example so we won’t do what they did, because they were destroyed. What is our end going to be? Murmuring: destruction. Idolatry: destruction. Out here fornicating and not wanting to change: destruction.

“Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.” You think you are standing in the truth? Take heed, because it is easy for this thing to fall backwards on you, easy to get caught up in idolatry, fornication or murmuring if we are not disciplining our spirit and our mind, steadily practicing this Bible, reading our four chapters and praying three times a day. If we aren’t doing these things, Satan is going to slide up and pull us back out, and it could be any one of us in here.

precepts.why:
All our fathers were under the cloud: what cloud? “The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light”, and “He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.”

That cloud is not a regular cloud. That cloud is a chariot God put over them. A video was shown, filmed live over the Dome of the Rock around 2011: lights at the bottom of a great craft, and a small one coming down and shooting back up to the bigger one sitting there. That is not a UFO; it is an identified flying object. We know what it is: a chariot of God, the divine vehicle of the Lord. That is how God rolls, in his chariots. The world calls them UFOs or the mother ship, but they are the chariots of God, whirlwinds, flying rolls: different names the prophets called them, names they could relate to in their time.

So when Paul says all our fathers were under the cloud, he means God had a chariot over us to protect us when we were going through the wilderness: a cloud by day to keep us cool in the heat of the desert, and a pillar of light by night.

All our fathers passed through the sea. “The angel of God, which went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them.” The pillar of the cloud was before them, then moved to the back of them, because the Egyptians were chasing behind the Israelites on their chariots, the little things with wheels they stood on.

“And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and it was a cloud and darkness to them.” They couldn’t see. It was dark where they were, but we could see where we were going. He kept us separated from the Egyptians the whole time, so they couldn’t catch up to us.

Then “Stretch out thine hand over the sea, that the waters may come again upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.” The waters covered all the host of Pharaoh, and “there remained not so much as one of them. But the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea.” “Thus the Lord saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.” The Lord was helping us out, going in front of us and behind us. As he delivered us then, he will deliver us out of this captivity now.

sense.text: You should not be ignorant: “I have also heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage; and I have remembered my covenant.” He remembers his covenant with us.

“I am the Lord, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.” He would redeem us “with a stretched out arm, and with great judgments”: he had great judgments on Egypt. “Ye shall know that I am the Lord your God”, Israel, your God, and he would bring us into the land sworn to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, and give it to us “for an heritage.”

“But they hearkened not unto Moses.” We didn’t listen, like today. This is spiritual Egypt we are living in right now all over again, and we are not listening even today to our Lord and Saviour, not listening to the Bible, not changing. Our people love evil, we love wickedness, we love entertainment; we don’t love God like we say we do. Them not listening to Moses was them not listening to the Heavenly Father, and them not listening to us is like them not listening to the Heavenly Father, because we are the messengers he is sending in these last days to wake them up, redeem them from the evil they have been in, and help them become a new person in Christ, with a new spirit and a new mind. Our people are crazy: we find every excuse to do evil.

“For anguish of spirit”: they had a low spirit, a broken spirit. Egypt broke their spirit, and that is what is happening today. A lot of people in this truth have broken spirits, and they run easily back out into the world because they find it safe there: safe in the hand of the enemy, the oppressor, following the heathen, first and foremost Esau, and after that the rest of the heathen, the Moabites, the Ishmaelites. They feel safe following them instead of coming back, following the Lord and this Bible, and coming back to who they are as Israelites. They get comfortable.

Anguish is severe mental or physical pain. That is PTSD: what we had then when we came out of Egypt, and what we have here in America. Our minds are gone, broken and fragile, and we haven’t noticed it yet; we have a mental problem and a physical problem we haven’t dealt with. That is why we deal with our problems through this Bible. “And for cruel bondage.”

precepts.why:
Anything we are going through, the answers are in the Bible. Not in the Quran: you never heard of a New International Quran; they don’t tamper with that Quran because there is no truth in there, no history, no prophecies, nothing that tells you who you are or who the people of the past are. No other book on the earth is more powerful than the Bible. It gives history, present time and future prophecies all through it, and that is why they are scared for us to read our book: the solutions are in this book, because we are the people of this book.

“According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness.” God’s divine power has given it to the Israelites. Not some things, not 99 percent: all things that pertain to this life you are living right now. Everything is in this book. Depressed, it is in here; anxiety, it is in here; suicidal thoughts, he tells you how to get around it. Mourning for somebody who passed, or your faith is low, he has it in here: how to build your faith, exalt you and comfort you through his words. That is what Romans 15:4 says: through patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.

We are broken people; God says we are broken. “Hope deferred maketh the heart sick”: that is the broken spirit, the mental distress and physical distress we are going through. You want something, you are looking for something, but if you are in the world you are not going to find it. You are looking for change, you go to politics and voting, and it is not there. You go to all these nonprofit organizations, Jesse Jackson, Al Sharpton and all these people: none of these things are going to help you. You have to come back to your Bible to get the help you need. Looking for change where it is not makes your mind sick, distressed and aggravated; it messes with your mind.

“But when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.”

“Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more”: we are going to keep revolting more and more against our Father. “The whole head is sick”: all our leaders out there in so-called displaced America, all the leaders we are supposed to look up to, are messed up. None of them have solutions for our problems. None of them come into the ghettos to help our people or build our people back, and even the people who have money don’t come back to their communities to build them up.

“And the whole heart faint”: your mind is weary, distressed, broken. That is why we have to go back to this Bible and rebuild our spirits. We have to get our minds right, Israel, and trust back in the Lord and in our record book that God gave us.

sense.text:
“For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine”: our people will not want to hear the truth. They don’t want to hear your mouth, don’t want to hear Christ, don’t want to hear about change or that they could do better.

“But after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears.” Somebody is going to come in and say, well, you know, we are still in the Old Testament, we ain’t in the New Testament yet, and they say, that makes sense, I’m going to follow you. And when you get out there, what are those teachers doing? Watching our classes, following us on the low. It makes no sense. Others want to hear that they can smoke weed because the Bible says herbs, herbs are from the earth; and you end up a damn crackhead, a cokehead, a dope head because you followed them.

“And they shall turn away their ears from the truth”: some of these sisters and some of you brothers are going to turn your ear away from hearing the right thing, because the lust of the world and the things of the world are going to pull you back, because you are not applying this Bible to your life. All through the Bible God warned us, and left those things for our example. So why would we tempt the Lord and play with him and say, that can’t be me, I’m stronger than that? That is how the devil gets his hand in and pulls us back out: you think you are stronger than you are. That is why he said take heed lest ye fall.

“And shall be turned unto fables”: they are going to be turned to lies. They want to hear lies, smooth things.

precepts.why:
He covered everything in this Bible. “This is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of the Lord.” That is what Paul was talking about in Timothy: they don’t want to hear the law of the Lord, they don’t want to hear this Bible.

“Which say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things”: don’t see my evil, don’t tell me what I’m doing wrong, just let me live, I don’t want to hear it. “Speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits”: lie to me. Tell me I’m the greatest on earth, tell me I ain’t got to work, I can just run around, post up in a woman’s house and lay up all day. Don’t tell me I’ve got to get a job, that I’ve got to change, that I’ve got to stop smoking weed.

“Get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path”: y’all in purple, move away, y’all are making us look bad, teaching the truth about one wife, getting your household right, getting a job. The Christian church lies that Jesus Christ is not black or white, that he has no color. We are going to speak what the Bible says, thus saith the Lord, and stand boldly in the face of all our enemies, and we have black enemies out there too: anybody who goes against what God says is our damn enemy, and we are going to preach against all of them.

“Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon”: you love to be under these nations, under the white man. Then stay thereon, and don’t come around us. If you want to hear lies and fables and don’t want to change, get the hell away from us. That is what he is saying.

Our people love to hear lies. “Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.”

“Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure.” They are not going to change. That is why you don’t sit back and debate back and forth with some of these negroes; you are wasting your time. Show them a hundred scriptures and they say, no, it don’t mean that, because they want to stay where they are. To the pure, if it is pure to you, you hear it and say, damn, that makes sense, I can roll with that. If it is not pure, you find every excuse to lie and push it to the side so you can keep your wickedness. “But even their mind and conscience is defiled”, because they want to stay in whatever evil they are doing. So don’t be out there going back and forth with these idiots.

“They profess that they know God”: we know Christ, we know the Bible, let’s debate. If you know the Bible, what the hell are we debating for? Christ said go to the highways and byways and compel his people to come in, go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. If you know and you are not lost, we keep this train moving. “But in works they deny him”: in works they deny Christ, his Bible and God, “being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate”, void of understanding.

“For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world.” Demas forsook Paul because he loved this present world, and the others departed, Crescens to Galatia and Titus to Dalmatia. Those men were under Paul, setting up churches, building men up, carrying letters to Galatia, to Ephesus and all that, and they left and went back to the world.

That is why he said take heed lest ye fall: the Bible is not a game. God warns us before the storm; he tells us what is going to happen before it happens. That is why we are supposed to have the upper hand, and why this fight is supposed to be a little easier for us: he already told us what to look out for. But some people just love this evil and love this world.

sense.text:
He already told us what to look out for. “And the cares of this world”: wanting to keep up with the Joneses, thinking you are missing something. “And the deceitfulness of riches”: riches are deceitful and uncertain. You have a job, you are getting decent money, and your boss comes and says you can make 40,000 more a year if you just work on the Sabbath, and you think, you know what I could do with that money? I could help the school. How many times have we heard this? That is the trick of the devil, a snare trap of the devil. You won’t see that brother no more, because Satan dragged him out. That was a trick to get him out, because he was covetous; he wasn’t content with the things he had. Satan said, let me get him out of here; he wants money.

“And the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful”: the lust, the desire, of other things, and then they are no good to the fight no more.

precepts.why: What did God say about riches? A brother answered that they are uncertain, and another that those who will be rich fall into hurtful lusts and temptations. “But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare”: they get snared. That is why people go out there and get trapped: they are chasing money, chasing riches, chasing fifteen seconds of fame through the white man. “And into many foolish and hurtful lusts”: many. The love of money is the root of all evil, the love of that thing.

That is what happened: a trick of Satan. He said, you can make more money, and the person said, yeah, I can make more and help the school, and he dragged them out of this truth. But “whosoever is born of God sinneth not; but he that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not.” God protects him. If you are born of God you are not out there sinning wilfully, and God gives you a little hedge.

“And we know that we are of God, and the whole world lieth in wickedness.” This whole world we are living in right now lies in wickedness; everything in it is set up against us. They give you disability, food stamps, Section 8, numerous programs, and you say they are helping you out; but it is all a trick at the end, to pull you out and destroy you.

The woman who was nourished is Israel. At the time we were nourished by Egypt; now we are nourished by America, spiritual Egypt. That is why they give us all these programs and good jobs: to keep us down as a people, nourishing and feeding us. Now they are starting to take that stuff back, and many have no plan. We have a plan: the Bible. We are going to work, trust in the Lord and do what God says. The trap Satan set up long ago was, get the man out of the house, we’ll take care of you; and even when the man is taking care of his kids and giving her money, many women put him on child support anyway, out of greed, to hurt him. It is all a trick.

sense.text:
We were nourished by this place. This place takes care of us, feeds us, and is supposed to uplift us through their programs, their education, their politics. “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies”: first and foremost it starts with Edom, the red man, our enemy. Ishmael is our enemy; the Arabs, the East Indians, the Chinese, the Japanese: everybody outside the twelve tribes of Israel is our enemy, and everybody enslaved us. We are serving our enemy right now here in America.

“Which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”: that is how they nourish us. For food, for drink, for clothes, we have to go to them; you want tissue, you have to go to them. Just to drive a car you have to go to them for their license; they say it is a privilege. Death certificate, birth certificate, anything you need, you go to them, and they have to approve you, and they can easily take it away from you.

“And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee”: the enemy, the white man, put a yoke of iron upon our necks until he destroyed us, as we are today. How do you know we are destroyed? We have their last names. We get the worst food, the worst education; we can’t even get the things we need in our own community. We sign a petition to get a street or a block fixed and they do it when they want to. Esau puts in a petition for a park and they do it; computers for their schools, everything, they give it to them. We lack those things because we are under these curses and are being nourished by our enemies to this day.

precepts.why:
We have to be thankful that the Lord is a true and living God who hasn’t forsaken us, or they would have wiped us out. “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked”: the earth right now is in the hands of the wicked, and that is why they have power over everything, over the food. They don’t want people to have seeds in their food anymore: GMO foods, GMO chicken, fake chicken, fake steak, 3D steaks they are making now.

“He covereth the faces of the judges thereof”: that is us. “If not, where, and who is he?” If he isn’t the wicked one, where is he and who is he? If that white man isn’t the wicked one, who is, dropping bombs all over the place? And the news says this week’s color is lavender; the news is the basketball game, LeBron James thinking about retiring, a street festival giving out food: all things that distract us from what is really going on in the world. That is how wicked and evil he is: he doesn’t even want you to know what is going on. Over in Israel they are bombing the news reporters and nobody covers it, so we won’t see what is going on over there. He is the most wicked, evil person on this earth right now.

A lot of our people follow them and want to be just like them. “Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil”: that is what is happening right now. People see all this evil going on and say, oh no, those people are just defending themselves. They are scared to speak up. Where are our leaders? Where the hell are the churches, the top pastors, the top entertainers, the actors and actresses? Why is nobody opening their damn mouth against this damn evil? Some of our people are calling the evil being done over there good, like Floyd Mayweather speaking highly of them. People are scared to open their mouths because they will lose the things they have. If you can’t speak up, you should secretly be supporting us, secretly donating, making sure this movement grows, because we are going to speak up and show our people through the Bible what is going on. Purple and gold: we are going to speak truth.

“That put darkness for light, and light for darkness”: they put Satan in the place of Christ, with that white image they gave us to hold up white supremacy. They made all the prophets white, and you hear nothing about the black people. A picture of one of them was put up, smiling and happy, but you won’t see him come to us like that and shake our hands, and we are the ones who put our lives on the line day in and day out in the streets. The Lord is showing who is real: the real leaders, the real prophets, the real men of the Lord doing his work in these streets. He isn’t calling them; he doesn’t want them; he wants us. “That put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!”

sense.text:
We are going to fight the wiles of the devil and speak about the evil that is going on in this world. “For my people is foolish”: whose people? God says, my people. You know how heavy that is, for a father to call his son stupid, foolish? We are foolish; we ain’t got no sense.

“They have not known me”: how are we a group of people that don’t know our father? We walk around as orphans in the street, as bastards, purposely. A bastard, in the Bible, is a child with no father.

“They are sottish children”: stupid. “And they have none understanding”: they don’t understand what they are supposed to be doing, where they are, how they got there, how they are going to get out of it. They don’t understand their reason, their purpose, why they were born, why they are here; they don’t understand that they are Israelites called to change this world and change the minds of their people. We don’t understand how to work and build our communities and our youth up, how to set up programs for them.

“They are wise to do evil”: when it comes to shooting and killing their own people, they are wise. They know how to cook up crack with the baking soda, shake it up, make it a rock and sell it; how to grow the weed, dry it out and hang it up. They know how to do every type of evil. “But to do good they have no knowledge”: they don’t understand how to do the right thing, how to get a job and work and struggle. At least then you are honest: you don’t have to look over your back, you have integrity, you are not destroying your community. Our people have no knowledge.

“Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity”: it is better for you to be poor and have integrity, have honesty, not be a criminal, not be an idiot, not be stupid. “Than he that is perverse in his lips, and is a fool”: he that talks stupidness; what he says makes no sense.

“Also, that the soul be without knowledge, it is not good.” A soul is supposed to have knowledge in it. Think about the animals: from the time an animal is born it knows how to take care of itself, how to hunt, how to find refuge and shelter. How is it that we as humans have souls in us but no knowledge that follows? What knowledge is the soul supposed to have? The law, statutes and commandments of God are supposed to be in us. When they are not, we have no integrity to stand on.

precepts.why: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain.” Some people are just born in vain. They are born to die, born to be part of the two thirds, born to help us with this trial we have to go through while we are here on this earth. That is what God said, and that soul without knowledge is born in vain.

A soldier answered that the soul is supposed to have the law, statutes and commandments of God in it, and gave this scripture. “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth.” We are supposed to be seeking the law at his mouth, not at our brother’s mouth. The law of the Lord is supposed to be coming from our mouths to the younger brothers and sisters: that is the knowledge we are supposed to give to this next generation under us, the commandments, to build their minds and spirits up.

“The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he liveth.” You can’t do nothing with a broken vessel. It is like dropping a vase, gluing it back and putting water in it: it leaks from everywhere and doesn’t hold the water it is supposed to hold. As long as he lives he is going to be an idiot, born for nothing, born in vain. That is why the things written to warn us are to wake us up, bring us to life, exhort us, build our minds and spirits up, and put zeal and fire in us for the Lord: not just words in a book, not just sitting around feeling good like in the Christian church. It is supposed to bring change to your life, and make you understand that God is telling us about these people, so when you see them you will know who they are.

“If a skilful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add unto it”: oh man, that makes sense, I never heard that before; and he adds a scripture to help strengthen what was said. “But as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back”: he is mad as hell because he has nothing to add and doesn’t understand what it is saying, so he casts it behind his back and doesn’t want to hear it.

“The talking of a fool is like a burden in the way.” Two clips were played: one on how mentally exhausting it is to be around stupid people, to hear how they rationalize information and draw conclusions; the other of a man told that everyone in the room was now dumber for hearing his answer. It is hard to hear an idiot. That is why he said they are like a broken vessel: they hold no water. And that is our people he is talking about. He calls us sottish children; he calls us foolish. God knows who he created, and some he created in vain. Don’t get caught up around them and don’t let them pull you out of this truth, especially you sisters, when the fool rolls up to talk like he knows what he is talking about.

sense.text: “And they come unto thee as the people cometh, and they sit before thee as my people”: they sit there like they want to learn. “And they hear thy words, but they will not do them: for with their mouth they shew much love”: oh man, I love the truth, it changed my life, all praises to the Most High. “But their heart goeth after their covetousness”: their mind is somewhere else.

“And, lo, thou art unto them as a very lovely song of one that hath a pleasant voice, and can play well on an instrument”: when we bring out the scriptures it is like a lovely song to them, like Luther Vandross or somebody who can sing real good. “For they hear thy words, but they do them not”: they hear what the Bible says but don’t want to change. That is how Israel is: you hear what the Bible says, but you refuse to make any changes.

The things written before time were written for our learning, and these same people are back on the earth today with fringes and borders of blue on. “And when this cometh to pass, (lo, it will come,)”: it is going to happen, and today is the day they are back again. “Then shall they know that a prophet hath been among them”: because we are warning you to stay away from idiots, from people who are not motivating or moving your spirit, people dragging you down spiritually. Spiritual vampires; the Bishop calls it STD, spiritually transmitted demons. Stay away from them, uplift your spirit and build your mind through the scriptures. That is what we are here for. You will know a prophet was among you, because we are telling you what is happening now and what to stay away from.

precepts.why: They will know a prophet was among them. “Howbeit I sent unto you all my servants the prophets”: he sends us to wake you up, to let you know what to look out for, how to carry yourself in this walk and stay ten toes down in this truth. “Rising early and sending them, saying, Oh, do not this abominable thing that I hate.” We warn you: don’t do the things God hates, the things that piss God off. Don’t be murmuring, don’t be out there in idolatry, fornication or adultery, don’t be running around lying. Build your spirit and your mind up. Have a true forgiveness for your brothers and sisters in the truth, so you can grow and the Lord can use you as a good vessel.

sense.text: “Son of man, go, get thee unto the house of Israel”: go talk to my people, go warn my people. “And speak with my words unto them”: we are not supposed to be speaking whatever comes into our mind; we are supposed to speak out of this Bible. That is why we have to study and learn this Bible and have it in our spirit, so we can speak it.

“For thou art not sent to a people of a strange speech and of an hard language, but to the house of Israel”: we are sent to our people. Whatever state, city, island, country or continent you go to, you are going to the Israelites; go find the Israelites. This is speaking of other nations, the Russians, the Chinese, the Greeks, the Portuguese, the Spaniards; though even among our own we have to learn how to deal with those who speak other languages, like Creole, and build them up. “Surely, had I sent thee to them, they would have hearkened unto thee”: if he had sent you to the East Indians or the Arabs, they would have listened to God.

“But the house of Israel will not hearken unto thee”: the real Israelites don’t want to listen. We love partying, confusion, arguing, holding on to things. The Day of Atonement has passed, and leaders are going to be counselling people who bring up things that happened before it: that means they never forgave their brother or sister, so they are not going to be forgiven, thus saith the Lord. “For all the house of Israel are impudent and hardhearted”: we are stubborn and hardhearted.

“Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces”: that is why we go to the highways and byways, to the concourse places and the openings in the streets, and go back and forth with our people, because we love them that much, trying to win them over and bring them to Christ. “As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead: fear them not, neither be dismayed at their looks”: we get threats back to back in the streets, people saying they want to kill us, and we continue to do this work. Our people hate the Bible and hate God while they call themselves Christians, and they want to kill us because we bring them the word of God, “though they be a rebellious house.”

“And go, get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people”: go to the Israelites, those in captivity. When we go to these islands and these countries, we go to our people who don’t even know they are Israelites, who have been worshipping Cesare Borgia because the Jesuit priests and Roman Catholic priests went down there with Christianity, rosary beads and little green Bibles. We have to battle for their souls and tell them: you are the Israelites; you are in captivity on this island, in this country, because you broke God’s laws. A lot of people in America don’t realize it to this day: they say they are free while they pay income tax and taxes on their food.

Unto thy people: when you go to China you are not teaching the Chinese, and when we go to Africa we are not teaching Hamites. The Hamites are not our people; God made it plain and clear. Wherever we go, Mexico, South America, Central America, we are calling our people to repentance, back to God, whether Hamites are in the mix or not. It is our job to wake them up out of that deep sleep, that coma, to resuscitate them and bring them back to life. You brothers on the internet critiquing our videos could use that same power to teach somebody in the street.

“Speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear”: tell them what God says through the Bible. Our hands are clean: God sent us, we taught them, and we go back and revisit to build them up, because we are the prophets of God back on this earth again. We are not cowards; we are on a mission from the Heavenly Father, ambassadors of God sent to wake our people and do this work.

Whether they will hear or forbear, we are on a mission. “Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people”: that is the only thing we have to do. “But this thing commanded I them”: he isn’t asking you or begging you; he is commanding you. Where is his voice? The Bible is God’s voice. Obey my voice and I will be your God: I will look out for you, protect you, defend you, fight for you, take care of you and assist you when you need. Just follow my words. “That it may be well unto you.”

“But they hearkened not”: he gave them the blueprint of what they needed to do to get to the kingdom of heaven, and they didn’t want to hear him. They “walked in the counsels and in the imagination of their evil heart”, the things they were lusting after, as Mark 4:19 said: the cares of this world and the lusts of other things, and they became unfruitful. “And went backward, and not forward”: the Michael Jackson moonwalk. They went backwards from the truth, from the law and commandments. We are supposed to be running to it; they are moonwalking back from it. That is what Israel did, and what Israel is still doing to this day.

“Since the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of Egypt unto this day I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets”: he keeps saying the same thing. He sent his prophets to wake his people up, and he sends us out here to do it. “They did worse than their fathers”: we are doing worse than our fathers. We have more wicked gods we follow and more idols we worship in this place.

precepts.why: “He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.” He says, I know God, I’ve got God in my heart; he is a liar, and the truth is not in him. Israel hearkened not and did worse than their fathers, yet says, I know God: that is a liar.

sense.text: At the end of the day, realize that we have a true and living God who will help us as long as we are making our way back to him: he will make his way back to us. Even though we are a rebellious people, God still loves us. “Turn ye unto me, saith the Lord of hosts, and I will turn unto you.”

“Be ye not as your fathers”: we just read that we have done worse than our fathers. “Turn ye now from your evil ways, and from your evil doings”: if we want to get right with the Heavenly Father, we have to turn from our evil ways. Some act like they are holy and in denial, as if they have no wrongs and are perfect; but your thoughts are evil. Sometimes evil thoughts jump into you. “But they did not hear, nor hearken unto me, saith the Lord.”
“Your fathers, where are they?” All of them are dead, and we are back here today: we are the fathers from back then. “And the prophets, do they live for ever?”

“The world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.” It pleases God for us to go out to these corners, on these flyer missions, doing the missing-person work, marching, hitting the radio shows and podcasts. We don’t give a damn what man thinks. People say we do all that for nothing, for vain glory; what do you have on your record that you are doing? It pleases God for us to go out and wake up his people by any means necessary and build the minds of our people. They have to see us and hear us, their teachers, for them to want to change; they have to notice change in us to want to do it.

It pleases God because he is a merciful God: he is the one who has mercy on us and forgives us.

precepts.why:
When a person changes: “joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.” Over one. Twenty thousand, ten thousand people may pass us on the street; there is joy over one sinner that repents. And again, “there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.”

That is why it pleases him for us to go out there and teach the word, and why the flyer mission is so important. You brothers who sit down and don’t get out, even if you say you are not with us, if you follow us, print out some flyers and hit the streets. Give them to these dead Israelites so you can bring them back to life and wake them up. You men and sisters who call yourselves following us, print them right off our website, israelunite.org, in different languages so they reach our people wherever you are in the world. Don’t sit around waiting for us to do all the work; get out there and put your brick in as well.

sense.text:
We have seen how wicked Israel is, how rebellious we are and how rebellious the forefathers were. Now it is time to see how the Most High has mercy on us, how he will get us out of this condition and save us through his mercies. That is the only way we will make it to the kingdom of heaven: through his mercy, not because we are some great people, not because we have fringes and borders of blue on.

“Now I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance”: that is what we try to bring you to. You know what you do behind closed doors. Each and every one of us has an angel next to us who knows what we did; the Heavenly Father knows, Christ knows. “For ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing”: we don’t want to destroy you or quench your spirit. We are trying to fix you, not break you or keep you broken; to put you back together through correction, through rebuke, through the upliftment of the scriptures.

“For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation”: if you have a conscience in you, godly sorrow works repentance in you, so you can get the kingdom of heaven. You take the correction, fix yourself and build off it, and become better. Sometimes you brothers and sisters get mad when you get corrected, but we are trying to get you to the kingdom of heaven, and you can’t get there without being corrected.

“Not to be repented of”: not so you go back and do it again and have to get blasted again. “But the sorrow of the world worketh death”: if you keep doing it, the Most High is going to cut you off in your wickedness.

precepts.why:
Correction comes with the curses. “The Lord shall send upon thee cursing, vexation, and rebuke”: vexation is being irritated and aggravated; rebuke is correction. Correction is part of the curses, because we forsook our God. So you men who don’t like to be corrected don’t want the kingdom of heaven, and you sisters who don’t like to be corrected don’t want the kingdom of heaven.

“In all that thou settest thine hand unto for to do, until thou be destroyed”: what has to be destroyed? The old man in you, the one who wants to fight against the truth, to fight against correction because you don’t like it. You are going to get it, and you are going to enjoy the correction, because you have to go through it to get to the kingdom of heaven, to get the impurities out of you so you can become that perfect man, that perfect woman.

“Because of the wickedness of thy doings, whereby thou hast forsaken me”: that is why we have to be corrected and rebuked, and why you have to get that godly sorrow, so you can make it to the kingdom of heaven.

sense.text:
“If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray”: that is what we have to do, humble ourselves and pray for forgiveness. You want the kingdom of heaven? Humble yourself, take the correction and pray to the Lord.

“And seek my face”: how do you seek his face? Start reading your Bible and studying the scriptures for the things you are going through. Don’t sit there with a lying spirit reading something that has nothing to do with what you are going through. If you are a thief, go to the scriptures about stealing: steal no more. If you are an adulterer or a fornicator, go to those scriptures. Whatever you are is in the Bible; deal with those scriptures to build your spirit up, and build yourself up on your most holy faith.

“And turn from their wicked ways”, while you study the things you are dealing with. “Then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.”

“Now mine eyes shall be open, and mine ears attent unto the prayer”: when you are sincere, diligent and loyal to the Lord, he is going to hear you, because you will have that godly sorrow. He will know you are sincere in what you are praying for, what you are dealing with and going through, and he will help strengthen you, because he knows you are real and serious about it.

precepts.why:
Then will he hear you, and we all need the Lord to hear us. The Day of Atonement just passed: don’t go in bringing up old stuff. That means you didn’t repent to the Lord; you just had a day you fasted.

“For there is no man that sinneth not.” They always ask, do you sin? Yes, I sin; my thoughts are sin, I have wicked thoughts. Solomon already told us there is no man that sinneth not: each and every one of us has sin in us. “And deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives”: that is us, carried away captive.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves”: if we would just sit back and remember what we did wrong, the wickedness we carried out, and remember our Lord, pray to him and confess whatever we are dealing with. “Saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”: we have to say we have sinned. That is how the Lord will have mercy on you, when you confess your sin, your broken laws, the things you are dealing with. And pray: pray three times a day.

“Then hear thou their prayer”: there are stages you have to go through. First acknowledge the wickedness you did, then confess it to the Lord: I’m a wicked, perverse person, I broke your laws and your commandments, I’m guilty, Lord. Then he hears, “and maintain their cause”: help them in what they are going through, Lord, in this flesh, in the body of sin. “And forgive thy people that have sinned against thee”: we all sin and we all need forgiveness. People ask, Cap, how do you maintain? Second by second, not minute by minute, hour by hour or day by day. A thirty-second commercial is long; look at what you could get yourself into in thirty seconds. Fight second by second, to keep your mind clear and sober and on the lookout for the wiles of the devil.

“And give them compassion before them who carried them captive”: compassion upon us right here in America, in Jamaica, in Trinidad, in Mexico, in Puerto Rico, in Santo Domingo, where we were taken captive. If you want the Lord’s compassion where you are, humble yourself and pray for forgiveness. Don’t go back to your folly after we just got a new clean slate on the Day of Atonement; don’t bring up old stuff you never forgave while you want to be forgiven. The Lord is giving us mercy in this wicked and evil place; take it seriously.

sense.text:
Don’t take this for granted. A lot of people take this truth, his mercy and his compassion for granted. If they didn’t, it wouldn’t be all through the Bible; he is repetitive all through it because Israel easily goes back to sinning, back to their wicked ways, back to breaking the law and commandments, back to calling evil good and good evil.

“Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest ye fall”: don’t go away from his mercy, from this Bible, or you will fall. A picture was posted of a brother who was an officer in IUC, and he looked like a madman, his spirit gone. Be careful lest you fall.

“Ye that fear the Lord, believe him; and your reward shall not fail”: you are going to have your crown of life at the end of this. “Ye that fear the Lord, hope for good, and for everlasting joy and mercy.”

“Look at the generations of old, and see”: as Romans 15:4 told us, look at the forefathers. “Did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded?” Did anybody trust in the Lord, wait on the Lord, call on the Lord and get confounded? Not one. “Or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?” There is a question mark behind that: God wants an answer. You have to be a real true and living God to ask whom he ever despised. That is the mercy and compassion he has.

Then he gives the answer: “For the Lord is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering”: I have been longsuffering with you Israelites. You have been rebellious since I made you a nation, to this day, and I have been longsuffering with you because I love you. “And very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saveth in time of affliction.” He forgives our sins and saves us when we are going through trouble. He might not jump when you want him to jump, but he always comes through and saves you in the time of affliction.

If you are going through something, he set it up for you to go through it, to build your faith and your spirit up, to trust in him, believe in him, wait on him, cry to him and be patient with him. We pray and think it will happen overnight, and God says, no, I want him to go through it so he can trust in me, so I can make sure he is loyal to me, she is loyal to me, at the end of this, and I can give a crown of righteousness. That is what we are all fighting for.

precepts.why: “For in all things, O Lord, thou didst magnify thy people”: in all things. We have got to trust in the Lord. He magnified his people “and glorify them, neither didst thou lightly regard them: but didst assist them in every time and place.” He assists us in every time and every place. He always helps out, always answers our prayers, is always there with us. We depart from him; he never departs from us. We do something wrong and depart, and he is always there to help and assist us in a time of need.

“The Lord executeth righteousness and judgment for all that are oppressed. He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel.” “The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger”: he tolerates us; he is longsuffering, “and plenteous in mercy.”

“He will not always chide: neither will he keep his anger for ever.” To chide is to speak out in angry or displeased rebuke. He is not going to always blast us; he is going to build us up. “He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities”: if he did, we would all be dead. “So great is his mercy toward them that fear him. As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.” See the God we are dealing with, a true and living God who loves us: I will move it all the way away from you because you are my children; I will give you a new heart, a new spirit. “Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.”

“But the mercy of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him, and his righteousness unto children’s children”: that is why we are here now and know we are Israelites, because it went on from our fathers down to this generation, and down to the generations after you if he doesn’t return by then. So build your spirit up in this truth and teach your kids, your wife, your family. It is “To such as keep his covenant, and to those that remember his commandments to do them”: those who obey his voice.

“It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not dead, Israel. We celebrate Tabernacles tomorrow, the Lord’s will, and people make it because of his mercies. “They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” “The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him.”

“For the Lord will not cast off for ever: But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies.” The Lord is a merciful God, and we forget how merciful God is. But that is not for us to take advantage of or take for granted. It is to build your spirit up and let you know that if you do slip, the Most High is merciful enough to pick you up and forgive you. You shouldn’t want to slip, you shouldn’t be willing to, but if you do, he is there to forgive you.

The Lord is a merciful God: “I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.” Some people say, my grandmother went to church all her life, I wonder if she is going to make it to the kingdom of heaven; my grandfather ate pork till he was 102, I wonder if he will make it. We don’t know. God will have mercy on whom he will have mercy, and compassion on whom he will have compassion. Back then they didn’t know any better; now we know better.

We don’t know whom he will have compassion on among the people of the generations before us. We know this: we had better be keeping the law and commandments and applying them to our lives. If we want to make it to the kingdom of heaven, we had better do better, because we know better. “So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.”

sense.text: “But unto them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience”: he grants them return and comforts them.

“Return unto the Lord, and forsake thy sins”: he keeps saying it through the whole Bible. Some people in this truth are going to come for counsel after the Day of Atonement and bring up foolishness; some don’t know how to let things go, and some are not forthright about what they deal with. God is telling you now what you need to do to get the mercy and make it to the kingdom of heaven: he is showing you the blueprint for being forgiven. He is a merciful and loving God, with compassion for his people; he is longsuffering with his people and pardons his people. “Make thy prayer before his face, and offend less.”

“Turn again to the most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead thee out of darkness”: he will bring you out of darkness, from sin, from the devil, “into the light of health”: into Christ, because Christ is health. “And hate thou abomination vehemently”: hate it aggressively.

“Who shall praise the most High in the grave, instead of them which live and give thanks? Thanksgiving perisheth from the dead, as from one that is not.” You can’t give thanks, you can’t pray, if you are dead in the midst of your sin, as one that has no life in them anymore. “The living and sound in heart shall praise the Lord”: keep the law and commandments right now, praise his name and glorify him. Pray three times a day, anoint yourself, fast; do the things you need to do to overcome your sins, or you won’t make it. We won’t make it if we don’t continue.
“Therefore is God patient with them, and poureth forth his mercy upon them”: he poured it on us.

“He saw and perceived their end to be evil; therefore he multiplied his compassion.” He saw it, because we stay in this flesh. We still have that evil mind and those evil thoughts, and that is why he multiplies his compassion.

“The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of the Lord is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teacheth and bringeth again, as a shepherd his flock”: as the shepherd takes care of his sheep, the Lord takes care of us the same way.
“He hath mercy on them that receive discipline.”

precepts.why:
“And yet tookest thou not away from them a wicked heart, that thy law might bring forth fruit in them.” In the beginning he didn’t take the wicked heart all the way away, so that the law might bring forth fruit, works, in us. “For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born”: we are all born after Adam with that wicked heart, that wicked mind. “Thus infirmity was made permanent”, “so that the good departed away, and the evil abode still.”

That is why he made the law: so we would be able to overcome and fight this fight we are fighting, this fiery trial, these trials and tribulations we go through. He didn’t just take it away; he implemented the law. Now we have to prove ourselves if we want to make it to the kingdom of heaven, trusting on him, calling on him, depending on him. And because the evil abides still, he multiplied his compassion.

sense.text: “When a righteous man turneth away from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, and dieth in them”: when a righteous man turns away from doing the right thing, commits sin and dies in his sin. That is what we were just reading in Sirach: you can’t praise him from the grave.

“Again, when the wicked man turneth away from his wickedness that he hath committed, and doeth that which is lawful and right”, keeping the Lord’s commandments, confessing and repenting, “he shall save his soul alive.” “He shall surely live, he shall not die.” That is what the Lord keeps saying. Israel, we have to wake up: the Lord keeps blowing the horn, warning and warning Israel how to get right, how to come out of their sins, stay away from evil, walk right in his sight, do what is pleasing to him, and make it to the kingdom of heaven.

“Yet saith the house of Israel, The way of the Lord is not equal.” People say it all the time: if we have a true and loving God, why would he put us in punishment, through slavery, through all this, if he is supposed to be a righteous God? “O house of Israel, are not my ways equal? are not your ways unequal?” I will forgive you if you repent and return to me, and you shall surely live. But if you leave my righteousness, go do evil and want to stay in evil, you have to die. Am I wrong for that, or are you? You are the ones who broke my laws and my commandments and went against me, so I punished you. What the hell are you mad about?

Now he explains it, and that is mercy right there: he is God and doesn’t have to explain himself, but he says, I love you so much I’m going to explain it. “Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways, saith the Lord God. Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin.”

“Cast away from you all your transgressions”: why is God repetitive like that? Because he loves us. I’m going to keep saying it, because I know they are hardheaded and don’t listen like they are supposed to, but I’m going to tell them anyway. “And make you a new heart and a new spirit”: become a new creature in Christ; get rid of that old spirit. “For why will ye die, O house of Israel?” Why go from righteousness to evil so that I have to put you to death? “For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith the Lord God: wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.”

“I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel.” God loves us so much he is going to bring all of them down there and plead for us, and he pleads with fire. “Whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land”: they parted his land, Jerusalem, Israel.

“And what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon”: you Africans, Hamites; what have the Hamites got to do with me? “Swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head”: if you try to punish my children, I will put it back on your head and punish you.

“The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians”: the children of Judah, the southern kingdom, sold to the Grecians, to the white man, “that ye might remove them far from their border”, the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. “Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have sold them, and will return your recompence upon your own head.”

“Assemble yourselves, and come, all ye heathen”, “and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about.” “Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe”, “for their wickedness is great.”

“The Lord also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake: but the Lord will be the hope of his people, and the strength of the children of Israel.” He is going to be the hope of his people and the strength of us, his children, the children of Israel.

“Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers”: we can’t speak evil of any man or be brawlers. “But gentle”: be humble, “shewing all meekness unto all men”, righteous toward all men.

“For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures”: we were foolish once, partying, having a good time, “living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.”

“But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared”: after all that, after we changed, after we repented. “Not by works of righteousness which we have done”: nothing we did. We are not such righteous brothers that he said, I’m going to gather them because they are so perfect and holy. Not for our righteousness: “but according to his mercy he saved us.”

precepts.why:
Not by our righteousness: “For I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.” He gave Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba for us, “Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.”

“Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up”, “bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth; Even every one that is called by my name: for I have created him for my glory, I have formed him; yea, I have made him.” He is going to do all this for us. Even though we are wicked and evil, look at our people out there, he is still going to do it for us. When he died, he died for us.

sense.text: “Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you”: don’t think it strange when you have to go through it, because we have to prove ourselves. God has already been proving himself: merciful, compassionate, longsuffering, pardoning us for all our iniquities.

“But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings”: why are people not rejoicing? He said rejoice. We are not supposed to have dead spirits in here; we are supposed to be lively stones, finding joy when we read the scriptures, because we are reading about our forefathers, about ourselves, and about how we are going to overcome and get the victory over every nation on this planet, thus saith the Lord. “That, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.”

“If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.” Those that hate him speak evil of him: y’all believe in an invisible man coming back to get y’all out of your condition? Yes, I believe it. You asked me, and the answer is yes.

“But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters. Yet if any man suffer as a Christian”, as a follower of Christ, “let him not be ashamed”: we have the true and living God looking over us, fighting for us, defending us, loving us, taking care of us, nourishing us and pardoning us, day in and day out. “But let him glorify God on this behalf.”

“For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God”: judgment is going to start with us, the house of Israel, first; he starts with his own house. “And if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God?” What is going to happen to those who broke his law and commandments? “And if the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?” The righteous of our people are going to scarcely be saved.
“Wherefore let them that suffer according to the will of God”, keeping the law and commandments, “commit the keeping of their souls to him in well doing, as unto a faithful Creator.”
